Ras el Hanout — The House's Own Blend

Moroccan · Easy · Makes about 60 g (about ½ cup)

Jump to Recipe Method Troubleshooting Storage
Ras el hanout — "the head of the shop" — is the spice merchant's own signature: the house blend, no two identical, every souk's version running its own count from a dozen to (the showman's claim) a hundred. This record is not the definitive blend (there is none — that is the blend's own doctrine) but the working house blend: the warm base, the peppery lift, and the two or three aromatics that lift the blend from the curry-powder's shadow.

Quantities live in the recipe card.

Ingredients

- **The blend's law: whole spices toasted, ground spices folded — never the reverse.** The base's pre-ground spices (the ginger, the cinnamon, the paprika, the turmeric) are folded in raw after the whole spices' toasting; toasting the pre-ground powder runs the burn's bitter edge in thirty seconds, because the powder's surface-to-heat runs a hundredfold the seed's own. - **The bridge:** this jar, the #91 harissa, and the #92 preserved lemons are the tagine block's three stones; the #97 tabil and the #98 dukkah are the blend's Tunisian and Egyptian siblings at the same cupboard's shelf. The corpus's "#94" citations (the mrouzia #41, the beef tagine #36, and the mqualli's #31 winter dial) all land on this jar.

Ras el Hanout — The House's Own Blend

Prep: 20 min · Cook: 10 min · Total: 30 min · Makes about 60 g (about ½ cup)

Ingredients

Ingredients

  • The warm base: 2 tbsp ground ginger (about 12 g), 2 tsp ground cinnamon (about 6 g), 2 tsp sweet paprika (about 6 g), 1 tsp turmeric (about 3 g)
  • The peppery lift: 1 tsp black peppercorns (about 3 g), ½ tsp cumin seeds (about 2 g), ½ tsp coriander seeds (about 2 g)
  • The aromatics' council (the blend's own signature — choose at least two): 2 cloves, 1 cardamom pod's seeds, 1 small dried bay leaf, ¼ tsp fenugreek seeds (about 1 g), and the luxury's option: 6 saffron threads (about 0.1 g) or a 2 cm cassia curl
  • The optional heat: ¼ tsp cayenne (about 1 g)

Instructions

  1. **The whole spices' toast (5–7 minutes).** The peppercorns, cumin, coriander, cloves, cardamom, bay, fenugreek, and cassia (if used) toasted dry in the heavy pan over the medium-low — the pan's steady swirl, the spices' movement constant — to the fragrance's first full rising and the seeds' faint deepening: the cumin's and coriander's warm toast, the pepper's first sneeze's provocation. Checkpoint — the toast's edge, the blend's whole gamble: the fragrance's first peak is the pan's off-moment — the 2–3 minute window between the raw's flatness and the scorch's bitterness — and the nose's own honesty runs the clock better than any timer: the moment the blend's perfume fills the kitchen's air is the moment the pan leaves the flame.
  2. **The cool and the grind.** The toasted spices cooled 5 minutes on the plate (the grind's own mercy — the warm seed's gum in the mill) and ground fine with the saffron (if used): the mortar's ten minutes or the spice mill's three bursts of five seconds each. Checkpoint — the grind's proof: the powder's even fineness at the rub between the fingertips — the coarse's grit at the tongue's edge runs the finished pot's speckle and the uneven blend's hot spots; the blend's whole evenness begins at this grind.
  3. **The fold.** The ground aromatics folded through the pre-ground base (the ginger, cinnamon, paprika, turmeric, and the cayenne's option) in the bowl — the whisk's full minute, the blend's every part meeting every other. Checkpoint — eating test (the warm milk's test, the blender's own ritual): a pinch of the blend stirred into the warm milk's sip — the warmth's round register (the ginger-cinnamon's body), the pepper's gentle lift at the swallow's end, the aromatics' council's perfume rising behind — no single spice's dictatorship, the cardamom or the clove never shouting over the blend's whole. It should taste like the shop's own front shelf — the house's name written in spice.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Blend bitter at the potThe scorch's toastThe nose's clock — the first peak's off-moment
Blend's perfume faint by the monthThe pre-ground base's ageThe small-batch law — the blend's 60 g made monthly
One spice's dictatorshipThe council's imbalanceThe clove's and cardamom's sparing law

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

- The blend keeps its full self for 1 month in the sealed jar's dark cool, its working decline honest through the third — the small-batch law is the blend's own: the 60 g made fresh monthly beats the year's jar bought at the showman's stall. The variations: the mrouzia's sweet dial (the cinnamon's doubling, the rose's petals), the lamb-focused blend (the fenugreek's and the cardamom's generosity), the Djerba school's hotter hand.
